A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LSC framework and VLM alignment study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite journal reformatting and the new Appendix O.

before.justification: V3 reports original VLM evaluations, fine-tuning experiments, ablations, and transfer results on Bongard tasks, Winoground, and VQA benchmarks.

after.justification: V4 retains those empirical results and adds synthetic retrieval simulations and Phi-3.5 noise-robustness experiments in Appendix O.

M1.justification: The nearest-centroid diagnostic, embedding aggregation, PEFT procedures, combined contrastive/next-token objective, and dual cosine schedule are retained. The revised image-to-prototype wording clarifies the existing centroid loss; noise injection is an evaluation intervention.

E1.justification: Appendix O adds synthetic random-vector retrieval and corrupted-embedding test scenarios on Bongard-HOI and Winoground. The original Bongard, Winoground, and VQA benchmark coverage remains.

E2.justification: The evaluated VLMs, CLIP and random baselines, and PEFT comparators remain. Gemma3 27B disappears from Table 1's selected summary, but its corresponding comparison remains in Table A.3. The noise experiments reuse the baseline and existing LoRA objectives.

E3.justification: Appendix O introduces inference-time Gaussian perturbations at the projector output, synthetic retrieval over a vocabulary of 2^20 vectors, and sweeps over noise, sequence length, and dimensionality. Existing splits and checkpoint-selection procedures are retained; the latter move from Section 3 to Appendix G.

E4.justification: V4 adds a focused robustness study testing whether prototype averaging resists noise, how this depends on sequence length versus dimensionality, and whether generative and probe performance deteriorate together. Earlier prompt-robustness, adapter-location, loss-sensitivity, and attention analyses remain.

E5.justification: The new synthetic retrieval experiment explicitly reports averaging over 100 trials. Existing seed references, confidence-interval reporting, and significance tests are retained; the PDFs do not establish increased run counts for earlier experiments.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark tables retain their numerical results. Figure A.4 and Table A.10 add noise-response findings: at noise 0.4, HOI generative accuracy is 75.2% for combined-loss LoRA and 70.9% for next-token-only LoRA. V4 also newly reports that newer libraries resolve Gemma's chance-level final-probe behavior.

T1.justification: Appendix O adds the stochastic definition e_tilde = (1-alpha)e + alpha n, with standard Gaussian noise and independent token perturbations. This is a limited formal addition; existing LSC, loss, and scheduling mathematics remains unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract recasts the task scope from abstract binary classification to compositional reasoning, while the conclusion qualifies the transfer claim as applying to out-of-distribution compositional reasoning tasks. The alignment-gap, two-pathway, and contrastive-training contributions remain.

C2.justification: V4 adds an interpretation of prototype robustness, explicitly distinguishes missing perceptual knowledge from alignment failure, and expands limitations concerning prompt placement and general VQA. It qualifies Gemma's collapse as environment-dependent, although Appendix Q retains the earlier architectural explanation.

D1.justification: V4 adds code/model access information and identifies the TalTech HPC centre. It flags Gemma's library dependence without naming versions. Appendix I removes the explicit model-specific values attached to the cosine scaling constant C, although the earlier hyperparameter-search values remain.

R1.justification: Related work adds Xiong's lattice representation hypothesis and the noise/cross-modal alignment works by Nukrai et al. and Zhang et al. It removes the PCC-tuning ceiling analogy. Several other reference changes update existing works rather than introduce new citations.

P1.justification: V4 condenses introductory, related-work, and methodology passages, expands the discussion, and relocates evaluation details to Appendix G. It removes the LLM-usage section and adds acknowledgments. The principal narrative sequence remains intact.

P2.justification: The journal conversion changes typography, title formatting, spacing, and page layout throughout. Table A.3 is enlarged across two pages, Table 1 is shortened, captions are revised, and Figure A.4/Table A.10 are added. Existing plot images are identical; their resizing and later renumbering do not represent new results.

improvement.justification: The new robustness evidence, clearer limitations, code/model access information, and more readable baseline table provide limited quality gains. The Gemma caveat usefully qualifies an earlier interpretation, but unspecified library versions and the unchanged architectural account in Appendix Q leave that correction incomplete.
